hook: SCP-7000 opens as a planet-wide breakdown of probability and quickly narrows onto one extremely unlucky researcher at Site-43. It is long and mostly a comedy, full of slapstick field missions and dry O5 banter, but give it time: the jokes are setting up something more personal. Its tags list a large cast of named Foundation staff, though the story introduces everyone you need.
whyItMatters: It shows how a K-class, world-ending scenario can be told almost entirely through one ordinary, unglamorous man and the colleagues who talk about him. The file is crowded with cameos from elsewhere in the setting, folded into running lists of absurd probability failures, which reward readers who recognize them without blocking those who don't. Underneath the gags it is a character study about being the butt of the joke.
thingsToNotice:
The early line calling SCP-7000-1 inconsequential is a planted joke that the ending pays off; follow the interviews with Wettle's friend, ex-wife and assistants and you learn that the site's accident log is empty and that Site-43 has always been unusually lucky, so he is not cursed but soaking up everyone else's misfortune. The Foundation then straps him to a task force as a living lucky charm, and the slapstick turns bleak as he breaks down, runs away and is hauled back.

The reveal comes through his parents: under mnestics his mother recalls the twelve-year-old Wettle praying, while she had lung cancer, that the universe take everything good from him instead of her. Decades later, lonely as his friends paired off, he drunkenly asked out loud for change, and the whole crisis was that wish breaking the old deal. He ends it himself by renegotiating, and in the bar he also pries loose the blacked-out surname of Dan.

Meanwhile the Chaos Insurgency collapses almost entirely offstage, its mobile array blown up by its own nuke, and the two drafted files at the end deliver the punchline: the public record blames an Insurgency device, while the real SCP-7000 entry names Wettle, who is responsible for his own containment.

related.note: The sentinel near the Sun whose eight-armed confusion and wave become clues in this file.
The pit of Sloth's Pit, which loses and then regains its bottomlessness during the event.
